title: Traversing Arrays with Loops
learningObjectives: Traverse arrays with index-based and range-based loops.
Compare indexed access with direct element iteration.
Accumulate and calculate values from elements.
Trace loop boundaries and iteration counts.
Avoid unsigned reverse-loop underflow and off-by-one errors.

understand.concept: Traversal visits elements in sequence. Indexed loops expose position; range-based loops visit values directly when index is not needed.
understand.whyItMatters: Traversal is the basis of totals, searching, output and filtering.
understand.explain: Keep index bounds strict and trace each visited item.

examples.title: Reverse traversal
examples.explanation: A signed index counts down through valid indexes.

practise.guidedTask: For Traversing Arrays with Loops, trace each example and record the collection type, size/capacity where relevant, valid index range, values before and after each operation, and what the code prints. Identify the key boundary case.
practise.independentTask: Write a C++ mini-task focused on Traversing Arrays with Loops: use a small collection of values/text, perform at least three meaningful operations, and test normal, empty or boundary, and invalid-index/input cases. Explain your collection choice and expected output.
hints: Select the collection type and justify its size behavior.
Trace initialization and current element values.
Use bounds-aware access for potentially invalid indexes.
Prefer direct traversal when the index is not required.
Test empty, first, last and out-of-range scenarios.
